key_headlines.title: Korea Development Institute projects economic improvement centered on semiconductors amid inflation and employment concerns
key_headlines.summary: The KDI forecasts improved economic conditions driven by semiconductor sector strength, with consumer spending rising due to increased auto and home appliance sales. However, inflation remains elevated and employment conditions are weakening.

key_headlines.title: Bank of Korea weighs additional rate hike despite inflation dropping to 2% due to elevated core inflation
key_headlines.summary: Despite headline consumer inflation declining to 2% in July, the BOK remains cautious as core inflation is accelerating. Governor Shin Hyang-sung emphasizes the importance of core inflation over headline figures for long-term monetary policy decisions.

key_headlines.title: Seoul apartment leasing crisis deepens as monthly rental contracts surpass jeonse for first time, exceeding 55%
key_headlines.summary: Seoul experienced a historic shift in the rental market with monthly rent contracts reaching 9,954 units compared to jeonse (long-term deposit leasing) at 8,114 units in June. The shortage of jeonse contracts reflects structural changes in Seoul's housing market.

key_headlines.title: Young and elderly investors face loan delinquency surge following stock market plunge from leveraged trading
key_headlines.summary: Delinquency rates on margin loans reached 0.22% across major banks, with alarming rates of 0.33% for those under 30 and 0.37% for those over 60. Approximately 63% of semiconductor stock-backed margin loans are held by elderly investors.

key_headlines.title: Seoul faces worst apartment supply crisis in 36 years with only 18,273 units scheduled for completion in 2026
key_headlines.summary: Seoul's apartment supply reached its lowest level since 1990, with only 32 of 336 redevelopment and reconstruction projects currently under construction. Experts attribute the shortage to stricter safety standards and excess profit taxes implemented during the previous administration.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy is showing improvement centered on the semiconductor sector, with increased consumer spending driven by auto and appliance sales. Current account surpluses continue to expand due to favorable exports. However, inflation remains a key concern despite headline consumer prices dropping to 2% in July, as core inflation is accelerating. Employment conditions are weakening, creating uncertainty about the recovery's sustainability. The KDI has characterized recent improvements as more positive than previously anticipated gradual improvement.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Real gross national income (GNI) grew 3.6% quarter-over-quarter and 15.6% year-over-year in the second quarter, exceeding GDP growth and reaching the highest level since 1988. The Bank of Korea is contemplating additional rate hikes despite inflation moderating to 2%, focusing on core inflation trends and second-order effects from demand-side pressures. International investment banks have raised Korea's average economic growth forecast to 3.2% for 2026. If the current exchange rate around 1,410 won per dollar is maintained, Korea could achieve per capita GDP of $40,000 for the first time. Europe faces record heat damage impacting both growth and inflation, with Germany potentially seeing 0.3% reduction in GDP growth and Hungary's nuclear power constraints affecting economic output.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean stock market showed mixed signals with the KOSPI experiencing volatility correction, while the KOSDAQ recovered to the 850 level driven by biotech and materials sectors. Market sentiment shifted as expectations for September Federal Reserve rate hikes weakened, with probability of rate hold rising to 55.6% versus 44.4% for increases. Bloomberg analysis suggests extreme market volatility has been stabilized through forced deleveraging and regulatory strengthening. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are considering large-scale shareholder returns amid semiconductor sector momentum. Top 1% retail investors are shifting portfolios away from semiconductor stocks toward batteries and biotech companies like POSCO Future M and Alteogen.
sections.Industry & Technology: The government is integrating non-aerospace companies specializing in AI semiconductors, solar cells, batteries, and cooling technology into the space industry through a 'K-Space Data Center' initiative. Global automotive markets show distinct regional preferences with Europe and Asia favoring electric vehicles while the US market increasingly prefers hybrid vehicles with double-digit growth. GS Construction and LS Electric signed a strategic partnership to strengthen power infrastructure competitiveness for AI data centers, focusing on next-generation DC power distribution technology. 17 companies including 6 AI fabless firms, 4 solar and battery companies, and 5 satellite system developers participated in government coordination sessions.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's jeonse (long-term deposit lease) market faces critical shortage as monthly rental contracts surpassed jeonse transactions for the first time, with monthly leases comprising 55% of apartment contracts. Seoul's apartment completion volume reached its lowest level in 36 years at 18,273 units in 2026, with only 9.5% of redevelopment and reconstruction projects currently under construction. Real estate prices are shifting toward the 9-20 billion won range, with nearly half of transactions in the 12-20 billion won segment achieving record prices. New tax reform rules will change how joint property owners calculate comprehensive real estate taxes starting next year, with potential savings through separate individual filings rather than household declarations.
sections.International Economy: The U.S. Federal Reserve is expected to maintain interest rates at 3.50-3.75% in September amid mixed inflation signals, with market dynamics shifting toward rate holds. The Trump administration is reshaping political and economic landscapes with strategic AI and trade policy changes, including eased China AI semiconductor export restrictions and increased federal contract awards. A Korea-Japan anti-dumping trade conflict has emerged in the steel sector, with Korean steel exports to Japan valued at approximately 300 billion won annually facing high tariffs. Global economic growth continues to decelerate amid Middle East instability, elevated oil price risks, and potential rate hike pressures. The Trump administration is taking a measured approach toward Iran tensions with a stated 'low-key' response strategy.
sections.AI & Economy: Eric Brynjolfsson, director of Stanford University's Digital Economy Research Institute, will deliver keynote remarks at next month's World Knowledge Forum, emphasizing that AI productivity is emerging from the depths of a J-curve with steep growth ahead. GS Construction and LS Electric established a strategic partnership to strengthen power infrastructure for AI data centers, with plans to jointly develop next-generation DC power distribution technology and establish regular technical exchange sessions. The power supply efficiency and infrastructure have become critical competitive factors for AI data center operations. AI-driven economic revolution is accelerating with major infrastructure investments from hyperscale companies entering a capital-intensive phase.
sections.Others: Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon met with young AI startup executives to experience AI technology and discuss the sector's development. Premium baijiu (high-grade Chinese liquor) imports surged 19.8% in the first five months of 2026 to $8.416 million, driven by popular brands like Moutai and Shunjufang amid overall liquor market downturn. Han Investment Management held an ETF new listing seminar, recommending long-term investment strategies in U.S. big tech companies and Korean manufacturing leaders for capitalizing on the AI era. Analysts argue that while the U.S. may be declining relatively, China cannot assume global hegemony due to underlying protectionism and nationalist pressures emerging in American society.
